presentation_summary: 53-year-old Asian man presented with one week of fever, chills, left upper quadrant pain, and generalized weakness, with a syncopal episode.
Two weeks before symptoms he had hiked in Harriman State Park in New York; he had no major past medical history aside from remote cholecystectomy.
Exam showed temperature 38.8 degC, conjunctival pallor, jaundice, and left upper quadrant tenderness.

Labs showed hemoglobin 11.2 g/dL, WBC 5.3 x10^9/L, platelets 90 x10^9/L, AST 38 U/L, ALT 62 U/L, alkaline phosphatase 270 U/L, total bilirubin 2.6 mg/dL, indirect bilirubin 1.4 mg/dL, LDH 279 U/L, and haptoglobin <8 mg/dL.
CT abdomen showed multiple wedge-shaped splenic infarcts with small perisplenic fluid; blood smear showed intraerythrocytic ring forms with approximately 1.5% parasitemia.
